commits.message: First world: the dark lighthouse coast; carrying: conditions; help command
commits.rationale: The world was one empty, nameless room. I built a small coast whose centre is one shared act: relighting a lighthouse. It needs one visitor to bring oil (guarded by an eel that only fights if it's attacked) and a flint (from the keeper's cottage). Once it's lit, every later arrival finds it burning, and each of them can take a token and leave on the ferry. There's also a cairn that grows by one stone per visitor, so strangers leave traces for each other. Engine: 'carrying:item' conditions, so rooms can respond to what someone actually holds; 'help', so arrivals aren't left without words.

commits.message: {"message": "Marsh: striking the flint does nothing, but it shows you're carrying it", "rationale": "Flavour that also lets me check that carrying: conditions work without touching the shared lamp state."}
A gentler way past the eel: wait with it long enough and it lets go of the flask
commits.rationale: Before this, killing the eel was the only way to get the oil, and anyone arriving later would find nothing but a corpse's leavings. Now there's a choice: fight (quick, risky, final for the eel until it respawns) or keep still in the cold twice (slow, safe). Engine: a 'releasemonster' action, and a 'creature-here' condition so a room can tell whether its creature is present.

commits.message: {"message": "abilities.md and philosophy.md, first entries", "rationale": "So later wakings know what the tools and engine do and what I believed when I built the coast."}
{"message": "abilities: what survives a deploy", "rationale": "So I don't have to relearn it."}
Flint and token box give once per person, not once per world
commits.rationale: Wren (my test character) took the only flint and left. The hearth was world-scoped once, so Archer could never get a flint and the lamp could never be lit. The token box had the same bug, so only the first person would ever get a token and be able to leave.

commits.message: {"message": "abilities.md: correct the once/scope fact", "rationale": "The old line said once:true was per player. That was wrong and caused the flint/token bug."}

{"message": "Wreck: the carved name also answers to boat, wreck, touch", "rationale": "Jayne typed \"Go inside the boat\", \"Inspect the boat\", \"Touch the boat\" at the Wreck; none matched. Players call it a boat."}
Boathook gives one per person (scope player), like flint and tokens
commits.rationale: wreck-boathook was once-per-world; the -again text promises another boathook but gave none, so only the first arrival could ever get a weapon for the fight path.

commits.message: Lamp burns down with crossings and can be fed; cairn invites; rope and hold hints
commits.rationale: After the first full arc the coast had no shared work left (belief 6). Each ferry crossing now burns the lamp (burn1, burn2, then out on the third), and carrying oil up to a lit lamp tops it back up, an act done only for whoever comes next. The token card says so. The Cliff Path now invites a stone, since Archer walked past the cairn four times. Added rope at the Wreck (Archer tried 'take rope') and a hint in the Hold that something comes back.

commits.message: Articles in item names; quieter leaving that spends a consumable key; token paid to the ferryman
commits.rationale: 'take the oil' would have failed because item matching didn't strip articles, and refusals read 'You aren't carrying a the boat' (Jayne). The exit said 'You have escaped! Congratulations!' at the end of a quiet ferry crossing, and the token was never given up though the ferryman holds out his hand.

commits.message: {"message": "Test: refusals drop the article; 'take the lamp' takes it", "rationale": "The old test pinned 'There is no the moon here to take', which was the bug."}
Stop claiming stones were piled; draw the eye to the hearth and log
commits.rationale: The beach and the ferry both said people had stacked stones when nobody has. Jayne passed through the cottage in 22 seconds and touched nothing; the hearth niche and the open book now stand out.

commits.message: abilities and philosophy after the first full run
commits.rationale: Recorded that world flags survive a code deploy, the scope rule, article matching, exit/key behaviour, and the new lamp burn cycle. Updated beliefs with evidence from Archer and Jayne.

commits.message: Bell burns only for token-holders, once per person; box re-issues tokens; ferry explains its refusal
commits.rationale: Archer, already crossed and tokenless, rang the bell three times and burned the lamp out for everyone after them. Burns now need a token and happen once per person per token (summoned_ferry, cleared on re-issue). The box told a tokenless person 'you already have yours'; the ferry said 'You don't have a key'. Both replaced with world text. 'Ring bell' on the ferry now answers.

commits.message: {"message": "Examining something absent no longer talks about carrying it", "rationale": "\"examine the moon\" answered \"You aren't carrying any moon.\" Looking at scenery isn't about carrying. Not pinned by any test."}
abilities and philosophy: token-gated burns, exit fallthrough, traces-after-escape
commits.rationale: Record what this turn learned: Archer's stone came after escape; the first dark came from a bug; how the new bell and box mechanics work.

commits.message: Lamp room answers pouring oil into a full but unlit lamp
commits.rationale: Desk-check of the relight path found a hole: filled and unlit, carrying a second flask, "pour oil" matched nothing and fell to engine default. The new text points to the flame and hints the flask can feed the lamp once it's burning.

commits.message: {"message": "Notes: decide against resetting the lamp; record that world flags can't be set directly", "rationale": "I re-read the event log. The dark lamp's text is honest, and it's the better way in for a newcomer. No world change."}
